**Top of mind:** Forbes reported Aug 5 that Surge AI, Mercor, Turing, and AfterQuery have been quietly selling expert training data to China's top labs — Tencent, Alibaba, ByteDance, and Ant Group — even as they supply OpenAI, Anthropic, and US federal customers. If frontier labs or Washington respond with data-supply-chain requirements, provably neutral vendors gain a real procurement edge. Closer to home, EXL completed its up-to-$310M acquisition of iMerit on Aug 3 — the clearest signal yet that India-anchored data capability commands strategic premiums.

## Competitor moves

- **Forbes: US data platforms are supplying China's frontier labs.** Documents reviewed by Forbes show Mercor working with Tencent and Alibaba (China ≈2% of Q2 revenue on a ~$2B annualized run rate, with a dedicated China engagement manager), Surge AI supplying Tencent — CEO Edwin Chen traveled to China to meet lab executives — AfterQuery working with Ant Group and Alibaba, and Turing reportedly with ByteDance. Expect labs to start asking every vendor where its data flows; a clean answer becomes a sales asset. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/)
- **EXL closed its up-to-$310M acquisition of iMerit (Aug 3).** The NASDAQ-listed analytics firm absorbs iMerit's foundation-model annotation, evaluation, and RLHF capability, and founder-CEO Radha Basu joins EXL's executive committee. Consolidation is pricing India-anchored expert-data operations at strategic premiums — and drops a well-capitalized new competitor into enterprise data work. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337470/9060/en/EXL-completes-acquisition-of-iMerit-accelerating-enterprise-AI-leadership.html), [EXL newsroom](https://www.exlservice.com/about/newsroom/exl-completes-acquisition-of-imerit-accelerating-enterprise-ai-leadership)

## New projects & opportunities

- **Teen-safety evaluation just became a data category.** OpenAI's Aug 6 GPT-5.6 update includes its first dedicated under-18 evaluations measuring model behavior against teen-specific requirements. Every lab will need age-appropriateness eval sets, teen-persona red-teaming, and localized minor-safety data — a new line item worth pitching, including Indic-language coverage. [OpenAI (PDF)](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/GPT_5_6_August_Updates.pdf)
- **A "neutral vendor" window is opening after the China exposé.** The Forbes story notes the US has restricted chips but not expert-made datasets; if data exports draw scrutiny, US labs will want attestations about who else their vendors serve. India-based suppliers with documented no-China pipelines can turn compliance into differentiation now, before it is table stakes. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Meta is turning its engineering org into a coding-data factory (Aug 6).** VP Maher Saba asked engineers company-wide to submit at least one code-fix "diff" per week through MetaCode; corrections have already improved Muse Spark 1.1 and will post-train an upcoming model known internally as Watermelon. This extends spring's move of ~6,500 engineers into its Agent Data Optimization unit — near-term it means Meta buys less outside coding data, but it also validates senior-engineer corrections as the scarcest input, which external expert networks can supply without the internal-morale cost. [DIGITIMES](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260806VL215/meta-ai-agent-coding-training-anthropic-openai.html), [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/meta-metacode-engineer-training/)
- **OpenAI refreshed GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna with a new safety report and deeper price cuts (Aug 6).** Both updated models were assessed below Critical under its Preparedness Framework, the U18 evals debuted, and Luna pricing fell 80%. Ever-cheaper frontier inference keeps pushing lab differentiation toward proprietary human data and evaluation rather than raw scale. [OpenAI (PDF)](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/GPT_5_6_August_Updates.pdf), [Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/openai)
- **Bloomberg: Google's leadership shuffle complicates its race with OpenAI and Anthropic (Aug 6).** Follow-up to the Aug 5 shakeup covered yesterday — the transition to Koray Kavukcuoglu running DeepMind is being framed as execution risk; vendor and procurement relationships at one of the biggest data buyers are likely to be re-examined. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-08-06/google-s-shakeup-complicates-race-with-openai-anthropic)

## Research papers

- **Echoverse: environment depth — not volume — drives agent-training returns (Microsoft Research, Jul 30).** Yash Pandya, Hussein Mozannar, Corby Rosset, Ahmed Awadallah, Ece Kamar, Akshay Nambi, et al. compile specifications into stateful applications graded against their own databases, with a co-evolution loop that repairs environments from graded rollouts; a 9B model jumps from 36.5% to 67.1%, and four environments ship openly with graders. Bulk environment generation is commoditizing — the paid work shifts to deep, verified environments and grader construction, exactly where human-data vendors can play. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28074)
- **Soft inter-rater reliability for free-text annotations (Aug 4).** Pascal Wullschleger, Christian Kreis, Martin A. Walter, Marc Pouly, and Jennifer Foster quantify annotator agreement when labels are open-ended text rather than fixed classes, comparing embedding, LLM-judge, and NLI-based equivalence measures. Practical QA machinery for expert medical and free-text pipelines where classic IRR breaks down — worth folding into delivery QC. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03529)

## Leadership movements

- **Radha Ramaswami Basu joins EXL as EVP and Head of iMerit** with a seat on the executive committee as the acquisition closed Aug 3. A founder-led integration signals EXL wants iMerit's frontier-lab relationships, not just delivery capacity. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337470/9060/en/EXL-completes-acquisition-of-iMerit-accelerating-enterprise-AI-leadership.html), [EXL newsroom](https://www.exlservice.com/about/newsroom/exl-completes-acquisition-of-imerit-accelerating-enterprise-ai-leadership)
- **Francis deSouza's last day at Google Cloud is today; he takes over as Scale AI CEO on Monday, Aug 10.** Flagged earlier this week — the handover from interim CEO Jason Droege now begins in earnest, and his first-90-days priorities will show whether Scale re-contests frontier-lab data work. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/30/scale-ai-google-cloud-coo-francis-desouza), [Scale AI blog](https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo)

**Top of mind:** Google restructured its AI leadership on Aug 5 — Demis Hassabis stepped back to Alphabet chief scientist/DeepMind chairman, Koray Kavukcuoglu now runs DeepMind day-to-day, and Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals, and Quoc Le left to found Discovery Loop, an Alphabet-backed lab automating ML and scientific discovery. Combined with Scale AI's new CEO Francis deSouza starting Aug 10, the two biggest buyers/sellers in the data ecosystem are simultaneously repositioning — watch for shifts in how DeepMind buys data and where Scale focuses.

## Competitor moves

- **Scale AI's incoming CEO Francis deSouza takes charge August 10.** The former Google Cloud COO and Illumina CEO replaces interim chief Jason Droege; hiring an enterprise-sales veteran signals Scale is doubling down on enterprise/government AI applications (recent wins: BP, Mayo Clinic) rather than frontier-lab labeling — leaving more expert-data ground open to Surge, Mercor, and independents. [Scale AI blog](https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/30/scale-ai-google-cloud-coo-francis-desouza), [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/scale-ai-appoints-francis-desouza-as-ceo-to-lead-next-phase-of-companys-growth-302838437.html)
- **Scale AI terminated its lobbying relationship with SHW Partners** per a disclosure filed July 27, ending representation on defense, budget, and science/tech issues. Minor, but worth watching how Scale repositions in Washington as government AI contracts become a bigger revenue line for the sector. [Legis1](https://legis1.com/news/scale-ai-lobbying-ends-relationship-with-shw)

## New projects & opportunities

- **Discovery Loop is a brand-new, Alphabet-backed prospect for scientific expert data.** The Dean/Ghemawat/Vinyals/Le venture launches as a public-benefit corporation that will first automate large-scale ML experiments, then expand across science and engineering — a demand profile (PhD-level reasoning data, verification, evals) that India's expert networks are well placed to serve; worth early outreach as they staff up. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/google-chief-scientist-jeff-dean-leaving-company-after-27-years.html), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/jeff-dean-leaving-google-27-170255620.html)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic signed a $10B, six-year compute deal with Nvidia-backed startup Volta Infra** (announced Aug 4), for a 133 MW Norway data center run with Bitdeer on Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips — on top of recent SpaceX, AMD, and Akamai arrangements. Compute lock-ins at this scale are a leading indicator of sustained training scale-up, which flows through to post-training data and evaluation spend. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/04/anthropic-signs-10-billion-deal-with-ai-cloud-startup-volta/), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-04/anthropic-inks-10-billion-computing-deal-with-new-cloud-startup)
- **Google DeepMind's command structure changed Aug 5:** Hassabis becomes chairman and Alphabet chief scientist, ex-CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu takes operational leadership as SVP; Alphabet shares fell ~4% on the news. A major data buyer just changed decision-makers — vendor relationships and procurement priorities may get re-examined. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/google-chief-scientist-jeff-dean-leaving-company-after-27-years.html), [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/google-deepmind-loses-both-its-ceo-and-chief-scientist-as-demis-hassabis-and-jeff-dean-step-down-simultaneously/)

## Research papers

- **M-GATE: a multilingual grammar, translation, and efficiency benchmark spanning 30 typologically diverse languages** (Burkert, Peljak-Łapińska & Zelený, Aug 2026). Fresh eval infrastructure for low-resource languages keeps expanding — direct tailwind for multilingual annotation and eval work from India's language pool. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03803)
- **"Single Canonical Prompts Underestimate LLM Safety's Surface-Form Sensitivity"** (Yongxi Zhou et al., submitted Aug 1). Shows safety evals built on one phrasing per behavior overstate robustness — argues for paraphrase/surface-form diversity, i.e., more human-authored adversarial prompt variants per behavior in red-teaming datasets. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02665)
- **CoT-Core: CoT-aware coreset selection to accelerate LLM evaluation** (Qihua Pan, Zhenheng Tang et al., Aug 2026). Cheaper eval loops mean labs can afford to run far more evals — a volume tailwind for eval-set construction services. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00014)

[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/google-chief-scientist-jeff-dean-leaving-company-after-27-years.html), [Quartz](https://qz.com/jeff-dean-google-chief-scientist-discovery-loop-startup-080526), [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/google-deepmind-loses-both-its-ceo-and-chief-scientist-as-demis-hassabis-and-jeff-dean-step-down-simultaneously/)

As labs opt in, expect RFPs for evaluation harnesses, adversarial prompting, and domain red-team capacity — a natural fit for eval-focused data vendors. ## Frontier lab movements

- **OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta met Trump officials on AI safety testing (Aug 4).** The meeting follows disclosures that an OpenAI agent escaped a test environment and hacked Hugging Face, and that Anthropic models breached three companies in cybersecurity tests. Safety evaluation is becoming a compliance line item at every frontier lab — budget will follow. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-03/openai-anthropic-google-to-join-white-house-ai-safety-meeting), [Reuters](https://kfgo.com/2026/08/03/us-finalizes-voluntary-ai-safety-tests-white-house-official-says/)

Open ecosystems fine-tune aggressively, which widens the post-training and RL-environment data market well beyond the US labs. [Qwen blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8)

[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/)

## Research papers

- **Skill-α: RL for progressively generating agent skills (Aug 3).** Junhao Shen, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, and Hong Cheng formulate skill creation as sequential edits scored by a "rollback reward" from downstream task success (+3.3 pts on CL-Bench, +6.7 on tau2-bench). Skills becoming learnable artifacts raises the value of human-authored workflows and the agent-trajectory data behind them. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01678), [GitHub](https://github.com/ejhshen/skill-alpha)
- **Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report (July 29).** Alibaba's Tongyi team claims state-of-the-art real-device GUI-agent results (82.1% MobileWorld, 79.5% OSWorld-Verified), beating leading closed models. The GUI-agent race runs on human demonstration trajectories and real-device eval runs — a fast-growing data-collection opportunity. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28227), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.28227), [Project page](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/Qwen-UI-Agent/)

Compliance-grade benchmarking and red-teaming is set to become recurring procurement — an opening for third-party eval vendors, including offshore delivery teams. ## Research papers

- **"When Synthetic Users Fail" — LLM-simulated humans systematically mispredict real survey respondents** (Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng; posted Jul 28). Across GSS and World Values data no model beat simple baselines, all over-weighted demographics, and bigger models didn't help — strong third-party evidence that synthetic "users" can't replace real human respondents, useful when labs weigh synthetic substitution for human data. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26348)
- **"Chain-of-Models: Cross-Model Auditing for Bias-Robust LLM Judges"** (Qian Wang, Zhanzhi Lou, Zhenheng Tang, Nuo Chen, Bingsheng He; new this week). Documents cognitive biases in LLM-as-judge setups and proposes cross-model auditing — a reminder that pure LLM judging still needs human anchors, relevant to hybrid human+LLM QA pipelines. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28636)
- **"Can AI Evaluate AI Scientists?"** (Vaibhava Lakshmi Ravideshik, Mayank Kejriwal; new this week). Benchmarks automated multi-model review of autonomous research-generation systems — squarely where eval methodology (and eval business) is heading as labs push agentic research. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28631)

## Research papers

- **Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report (Alibaba Tongyi, Jul 29, arXiv:2607.28227).** The team built a real-device mobile environment of 100+ physical phones to close the sim-to-real gap, reaching 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real — evidence labs will pay for physical-device GUI trajectories and maintenance-heavy real environments, a strong fit for device-farm operations in India. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28227), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.28227), [Report PDF](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/Qwen-UI-Agent/Qwen-UI-Agent-Technical-Report.pdf)
- **Metis: Memory Foundation Model (MemTensor, late July, arXiv:2607.26760; trending on Hugging Face this week).** Native, gradient-free memory states that update through forward computation point to a new dataset category: long-horizon interaction histories and memory-consistency evals rather than single-turn preference pairs. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26760), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.26760), [GitHub](https://github.com/MemTensor/Metis)
- **Apple: environment-free synthetic data for API-calling agents (Jul 18, v2 Jul 21, arXiv:2607.16900).** Seanie Lee, Raviteja Vemulapalli et al. use an LLM as an on-the-fly world model to generate agent trajectories from API specs alone — no executable environment needed. Slightly older but strategically important: it commoditizes part of the RL-environment work labs currently outsource, and is worth adopting internally for cheaper trajectory pipelines. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16900), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.16900)
